title: add transactional schema migration guard + backup/restore verification for private-installer
author: Ayesha Khan
release_notes: Adds transactional migration guard to prevent unsafe downgrades; enforces pre-upgrade backup and post-upgrade verification; pins installer component versions during upgrades to avoid accidental drift; small Helm and Terraform updates to support upgrade checks.
description: Motivation: private installer upgrades have produced a class of failures where schema migrations applied on upgrade made downgrades unsafe and produced partial state in customer environments. This PR implements a transactional guard around schema migrations plus robust pre-upgrade backup and post-upgrade verification and version pinning to reduce accidental drift. Summary of changes: 1) Add migration-runner transactional mode: run migrations inside an explicit checkpoint/transaction where supported and emit migration-manifest with applied migration IDs; 2) Add downgrade guard: upgrade-check step now records current DB schema version and refuses downgrade if target version < current and migrations have been applied; 3) Pre-upgrade backup hooks: installer now triggers a best-effort snapshot (Postgres pg_dump + etcd snapshot for distributed configs) and uploads to configured backup location; 4) Post-upgrade verification: installer runs schema validation queries and basic smoke checks and fails upgrade if critical checks fail; 5) Helm chart changes: new values.upgradeChecks.enabled, values.backup.enabled, and chart hooks for pre-upgrade and post-upgrade jobs; 6) Terraform module: add optional backup_bucket and upgrade_check_timeout variables; 7) CLI: redwood-installer inspect-upgrade command to preview actions and fail early; 8) Docs: upgrade runbook updated with steps and failure/recovery flow. Commits (high level): "init: add migration runner transactional support and manifest emission"; "feat: upgrade-check downgrade guard and version pin enforcement"; "chore: helm chart hooks and values for pre/post upgrade"; "feat: tf module backup_bucket and timeout variables"; "test: add integration tests for rollback prevention and backup verification"; Changed files (high level): "installer/migration-runner/*.go"; "installer/hooks/pre-upgrade-backup.sh"; "helm/redwood-private/templates/upgrade-check-job.yaml"; "helm/redwood-private/values.yaml"; "terraform/modules/private_installer/main.tf"; "cli/cmd/inspect_upgrade.go"; "docs/private-installer/upgrade-runbook.md"; "tests/integration/upgrade_flow_test.go". CI checks and status: initial CI run failed on lint and flaky integration test; fixes pushed to address lint (go fmt, docs) and increased timeouts for integration tests; final CI run: all checks passed including e2e upgrade_flow_test against a local clustered postgres fixture. Review conversation summary: Daniel Park requested explicit idempotency guarantees in migration runner and stronger tests around partial migrations; author added an idempotency layer and tests showing repeated runs are safe; Liam O'Connor asked for clearer failure semantics and improved logging for the backup hook; logs and metrics were added and a dashboard panel suggested; Sofia Martinez asked for a minor YAML formatting change to the Helm values and approval after CI green. Edge cases and limitations: for some older Postgres minor versions transactional DDL is not available; the runner falls back to a best-effort mode and annotates the migration-manifest; downgrade guard will still block in those cases unless operator explicitly passes --allow-unsafe-downgrade (documented and gated). Rollback procedure: the runbook includes steps to restore from the pre-upgrade backup and re-run migrations or restore previous release; operator-facing CLI prints clear instructions when a failure occurs. Backwards compatibility and version pinning: chart now includes a pinned component_versions block used only during upgrades to prevent mixed-version clusters during rolling upgrades; this lowers risk of migration/behavior mismatch. Testing and validation: added unit tests for manifest emission, integration tests that simulate failed migration to validate backup/restore path, and an e2e test against a 3-node local cluster. Merge outcome: approved by reviewers after CI green and squash-merged to main. Notes for release: recommend including these steps in Private release notes and scheduling a canary upgrade with a short maintenance window for early customers.
